heuristics: Pick the primary node by the paper's main methodological contribution, not the organism or disease it studies (a new spatial atlas of the tumour microenvironment is Transcriptomics > Spatial transcriptomics).

A paper that introduces a new assay, instrument or reagent belongs under the technique it advances; papers that only use routine assays take their primary node from the method that drives the discovery.
Combined computational-experimental papers: choose Computational or AI only when the model drives the discovery; otherwise the experimental method is primary and the computation is secondary.
Perturbation plus readout (e.g. Perturb-seq): the perturbation branch is primary when the screen is the contribution; the readout branch is secondary.
Clinical papers take their node from the study design (trial, cohort, Mendelian randomization); the disease belongs in the Application Tree.
Use the Application Tree (and the organism facet) for what the work is for; keep the Method Tree for how the work was done.
